author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: PKD's March 16, 1977 fan letter to psychologist Julian Jaynes, congratulating him on The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind, whose theory of god-voices PKD seized on to explain his own 2-3-74 experience.
page_summary:
On March 16, 1977, Philip K. Dick wrote to Julian Jaynes after reading The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind. He had seen the book reviewed in Time, hurried out to buy it, and, as he tells Jaynes, spent the previous night raving about it to his editor. Jaynes's argument, that early humans experienced the two hemispheres of the brain as a commanding god-voice and a listening self, offered PKD a naturalistic frame for the tutelary voice and sudden knowledge that had overtaken him in 1974.

The letter is a fan's congratulation, but it also marks a real turn in PKD's post-2-3-74 theorizing. Jaynes recurs in his later correspondence to Warrick, Galen, and others, and the bicameral-mind idea entered the working vocabulary of the Exegesis.

The item documents the moment PKD adopted one of the outside theories he used to interpret his own experience, in a letter to the theory's author.
